title: chatflow liaison: OpenAI Chat-completions mapping and streaming edge proxy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight runtime edge proxy that maps Redwood's chat API semantics to the OpenAI Chat Completions API (and back) with correct streaming behavior, function/tool-call fidelity, and structured output enforcement. This work addresses interoperability for customers who need to proxy OpenAI-compatible traffic through Redwood (for region/routing/fallback reasons) while preserving Redwood features: idempotency, token accounting, structured output validation, and observability.

Scope:
- Request mapping from Redwood chat schema -> OpenAI chat-completions request shapes, including role normalization, system/prompt handling, and per-message metadata (metadata gets encoded into message prefix when necessary).
- Streaming responses: support both SSE/chunked newline-delimited delta streams (OpenAI-style) and Redwood's streaming primitives. Implement adaptive chunking so Redwood streaming hooks (byte-level and event-level tracing) remain accurate across different downstream chunk boundaries.
- Function/tool calling: translate Redwood tool invocation schema (function definitions, arg schemas, call-mode hints) to OpenAI function call fields and map function call responses back into Redwood tool result objects. Implement coercion for mismatch in argument typing and propagate partial tool-call deltas correctly in streaming mode.
- Structured outputs: enforce output schemas (JSON/YAML/Protobuf-like hints) by post-processing returned text or by steering model via extra prompt wrappers where possible. Provide a fallback validation-and-rewrite step that emits well-structured errors with clear diagnostics for callers.
- Edge semantics: implement conversation watermarking and idempotent request tokens so retries and hedging do not produce duplicate outputs downstream. Maintain mapping tables for message IDs and token counters so usage reporting is consistent with Redwood billing.
- Error handling: map OpenAI error classes and codes into Redwood error taxonomy. Ensure transient errors allow safe retries with correct resume points for streaming.

Non-goals: full parity with all OpenAI behavioral corner-cases. We will iterate on high-impact differences only.
acceptance_criteria: Request mapping preserves roles, system prompts, and per-message metadata with <1% of test cases requiring manual coercion

Streaming path reproduces the same delta events order for 99% of synthetic conversations compared to direct OpenAI calls (within chunk boundary variance), and Redwood stream hooks receive consistent per-token timing metrics
Function call round-trip correctness: 100% of function signatures in our test corpus produce a correctly mapped call and the tool result is rehydrated into Redwood tool response format
Structured output validator rejects malformed model outputs and returns a deterministic rewrite or an explicative error payload
Telemetry: each proxied request emits mapping diagnostics (mapping_version, coercion_flags, downstream_request_id) and token accounting matches downstream usage within 2% margin
Rollout plan gated by automated canary tests and a feature flag with capacity-limited rollouts per-customer

Docs: API changelog entry and migration notes for partners

comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after PM sync. Goals and scope drafted. Referenced customer ask from AcmeCorp wanting to route OpenAI-compatible clients through Redwood for observability.

2025-02-18 Diego Rivera: Spiked an adapter prototype to translate roles and simple function calls. Found mismatch in how OpenAI encodes streaming function call deltas; will add a delta reconciler to ensure consistent function-call boundaries.
2025-02-21 PM review (Olivia Chen): Prioritize structured-output validator; several customers have strict JSON outputs and need deterministic failure diagnostics.

2025-02-25 Eng review (Kofi Mensah): Suggested adding conversation watermarking to handle idempotency across retries and hedging code paths. Also recommended token accounting reconcile job for end-of-day reports.

2025-03-01 Diego Rivera: Implemented request normalizer + unit tests for 120+ role variants. Streaming adapter basic e2e passing against stub (github.com/redwood/compat-proxy/pull/43). Marking as In Progress and starting security review.

2025-03-01 QA (Marta Silva): Started writing canonical fuzz tests focusing on chunk boundary permutations and tool-call delta interleaving. Found a case where a function call name is renamed by the model; we need a robust name-alias map.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Streaming semantics mismatch causes broken client assumptions (partial deltas interpreted as final). Mitigation: add explicit finish markers and windowed buffering on the Redwood-to-client stream for ambiguous sequences.

Risk: Function call argument schema mismatch may cause downstream tool failures. Mitigation: implement coercion rules + safe fail path that surfaces structured error to caller instead of invoking tool.
Risk: Token accounting drift between Redwood and downstream provider. Mitigation: incremental reconciliation job and conservative over-reporting flag until verified.
Risk: Security review for proxied tenants. Mitigation: require KMS-backed API key storage and per-tenant audit logs; block private data flows until compliance sign-off.
rollout_plan: Internal canary with 5 Redwood-internal teams for 48 hours
External pilot for two low-risk customers (opt-in) for 1 week
Gradual ramp with throttles and auto-rollback triggers based on error rate and token-accounting divergence
next_steps: Submit PR for structured-output validator (PR #47) and request API review
Schedule cross-team demo with SDK and Console teams
